reuse.why: All five month-wide actions, the new one included, go through the existing getBulkBudgetCategories, but the #fixed check uses its own whitespace split instead of the shared extractTagsFromText in #shared/tags, and the new action writes its own income/expense sign rule next to averageToBudget.

duplication.why: Category selection stays in one place; the only duplication is a second, simpler tag parser and a sign rule close to averageToBudget.

placement.why: The exclusions (templates, #fixed groups, hidden on request) are added to the shared bulk selector in budget/actions.ts, and the new action is registered in budget/app.ts next to the other month-wide methods.

scope.why: Mostly focused, but it reorders an unrelated import in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: Every exclusion is in one selector that every bulk action uses, but tag matching that differs from the app's own tag parser is a likely source of drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: budget/actions.ts getBulkBudgetCategories: cat.group_note?.split(/\s+/).includes('#fixed') instead of extractTagsFromText from #shared/tags

disguised_duplication.where: budget/actions.ts: the #fixed detection reshapes the tag extraction that #shared/tags extractTagsFromText already provides, using a whitespace split instead of the shared regex

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories keeps two options (includeHidden renamed to includeHiddenCategories, plus skipMissingGroup); the template and #fixed exclusions are general rules that apply to every caller, and all five bulk actions, setLastMonthSpending included, call the selector
